chunks: What is [the matter] with you that you do not believe in Allah, while the Messenger is calling you to believe in your Lord, and He has already taken your covenant, if you are believers?
ai.seo_question: Why does the Quran ask 'What is with you?' regarding disbelief in Surah Al-Hadid?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a rhetorical challenge to the Hypocrites (Munafiqun) in Medina, questioning their inconsistency between verbal profession and inner conviction. The 'covenant' (Mithaq) refers to the primordial or specific prophetic pledge) underscores the divine expectation of loyalty to the Prophet and, by extension, the Ahl al-Bayt, making faith a matter of both intellectual assent and practical adherence.
